newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices fall but spreads to bund narrow.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices fall but spreads to bund narrow.

text.p: Danish bond prices closed down on Monday, sapped by a dearth of buying despite well-received first quarter GDP data. But they fared better than German paper and the Danish-German 10-year yield gap narrowed.
"Denmark is doing well as a result of the good GDP numbers but that is overshadowed by lack of activity. There's simply nothing happening," a dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 ended the day at 112.40, yielding 6.11 percent, down from Friday's 112.50.
The seven percent 2007, due to become the benchmark on September 1, fell to 104.98, yielding 6.32 percent, from 105.20.
Turnover in the 2007 was a modest 1.9 billion crowns.
The 2006 bond's yield gap to the 10-year bund narrowed two basis points to 41 bp and the 2007 gap to the bund closed three basis points, to 61.
The crown firmed to 3.8068 to the mark from 3.8075.
The 2006 bond's September future closed down 0.08 point at 111.68, with five contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond, maturing in 2026, slipped to 90.70. from Friday's 90.90. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
